newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo trade likely dull, Hong Kong faces breather.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo trade likely dull, Hong Kong faces breather.

text.p: Investor caution ahead of results of a business survey is likely to curb buying on the Tokyo stock exchange in the week ahead, traders said.
The Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey is due out on Wednesday.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index, which has reached record closes in recent sessions, may face a correction but the market's momentum would limit any losses.
Wall Street's continued climb to new highs would help sentiment. The Dow industrials surged 50 points on Friday.
In Bangkok, brokers expect a rally as the political situation is clarified, with economic portfolios in the country's new cabinet likely to be settled.
Jakarta, Singapore and Taipei are expected to rise.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key index is likely to slip back into range-bound trade in the week ahead, as investors become cautious ahead of the end of the month.
"We probably won't see further buying from institutional investors next week as the end of the month is approaching," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Higashida expected the Nikkei average to hover between 20,500 and 21,500.

Most investors are expected to keep a low profile ahead of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey of business sentiment on Wednesday, which will indicate the state of the current economic recovery, brokers said.
On Friday, the key Nikkei 225 average closed at 21,216.11, up 286.38 points from its closing on November 15.
HONG KONG - A steady rise in Hong Kong stocks is bringing the Hang Seng index closer to a correction but market momentum could limit any losses in the coming week, analysts said.
"I think the market still wants to take a breather but it still has momentum to it," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.

The Hang Seng index gained 227.42 points, or 1.76 percent, in the past week to close at 13,116.79 points on Friday, up 17.23 points on the day. Analysts forecast a range 12,800 to 13,400 points in the week ahead.
BANGKOK - Thai stocks are expected to rally on expectations that a new Thai coalition under Chavalit Yongchaiyudh would agree on sharing economic portfolios, analysts said.
"I think there is some room for a short-term rebound next week," said Kanjanee Kornwanpornsire, head of research at Thai Fuji Finance and Securities.
Thai monthly economic data due for release by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday and the signing of a U.S.-Thai double tax exemption treaty should lift market sentiment, she said.
The SET index ended at 970.30 on Friday, down from 1000.73 a week ago.

BOMBAY - Indian shares are likely to continue to slide on disappointing first-half results, traders said. But they said a technical correction after the sharp fall in the past week could soften the blow.
Earnings announcements due include cement firm ACC and largest commercial bank State Bank of India. Both are index stocks.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index dropped 173.36 points or 5.5 percent to 2965.66 in the week to Friday.
DHAKA - Brokers said the market was likely to rise early in the week.

A market correction pulled Dhaka stocks down in all but one session last week and trading was suspended on Thursday after traders in the kerb market, panicked by the slump, assaulted a broker and battled with police.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) index lost 269.23 points at 3,298.04 in the week ending Thursday.
JAKARTA - Brokers and analysts said the market was likely to make further gains, boosted by the listing of Bank Negara Indonesia on Monday.

"Some banking stocks could enjoy a spillover effect from the BNI because many unsuccessful investors during the public offer period could pick the stock up from the secondary market," Motoo Murata, senior economist of Daiwa Institute of Research said.
"If they are still unsuccessful on BNI they could pick up other banking stocks," he said. On Friday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed at 612.86 points, against last week's close of 616.89 points.
KUALA LUMPUR - Analysts were divided over the possibility of the continued strong performance of blue-chip stocks.
"It may be fairly quiet. The Second Board index needs to consolidate some more," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities in Kuala Lumpur.
Week-on-week the Composite Index rose 25.80 points to 1217.96 from 1192.16 at last Friday's close. The Second Board index shed 43.84 points from 654.58 a week ago to close at 610.74 on Friday.

Analysts said there had been a gradual re-rating of Malaysia by foreign fund managers since the release of favourable economic data indicating a moderation of inflationary pressures, and an easing of the country's current account deficit.
MANILA - Philippine shares are seen drifting as a long weekend holiday announced for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit meetings keeps investors away, brokers said.
The stock market will stay open on Monday but "not many people will be out in the market because of the holidays", Julie Villena, trader at Dharmala Securities Inc said.
But better nine-month gross national product figures expected to be released next week could buoy the market.
The main index ended at 3,102.36 points on Friday, up by 40.26 points, or 1.131 percent, from the previous Friday's close of 3,062.10 points.

SEOUL - The market is expected to remain in the doldrums due to negative factors and no new incentives, brokers said. "Rising bond yields and a bribery scandal involving a bank's head will further dampen the already fragile sentiment," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
Brokers said key bond yields were rising due to high cash demand from companies, which have been suffering from worsening cash flows because of sluggish exports.
The composite index closed at 731.44 on Friday, down 2.5 percent or 18.85 points from last Friday's 750.29.
SINGAPORE - Singapore shares were seen staying on firm ground supported by liquidity from overseas buying interests.
Dealers said the Straits Times Industrials Index would keep nudging the 2,200 level after failing to pierce that resistance for two consecutive days in the past week.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index closed at 2,194.75 on Friday, against 2,193.64 the previous week.
"Liquidity has to continue for at least a week before we see a convincing move through 2,200," one institutional dealer said.
SYDNEY - Australian brokers saw the stock market as firmer in the medium term, although further losses in the coming week would not surprise after the bourse's recent run-up.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index ended at 2,383.4 on Friday, a loss of 3.9 points over the week. However, this disguised a buoyant week for the bourse in which it hurdled the 2400 barrier for the first time, peaking at an all-time high of 2406.2 on Wednesday before running into moderate profit taking.
"I think it will go higher in the medium term but it may weaken next week. It largely depends on the U.S. market," said a Sydney broker.

TAIPEI - Taiwan share prices are expected to rise further on momentum from recent sharp gains, brokers said. The index, gaining nearly 200 points in the past seven sessions, had broken a psychological barrier and is set to challenge 7,000 points, said Allen Huang, an investment manager at National Securities.

"In addition to the big gains, the market has been getting huge turnovers, which indicates very bullish sentiment," he said. The index ended at a 22-month closing high of 6,761.39 on Friday, compared to 6,587.44 a week earlier. A 6,700-7,000 range was seen for the week.

WELLINGTON - New Zealand shares closed slightly weaker on Friday after a mixed session, with the market turning its focus to the coming week when New Zealanders should have an inkling as to who will govern the country after weeks of coalition talks.

"Until we get some firmer indications from them I suppose it's going to be a little bit sloppy," Duncan Rutherford at ANZ Securities said. "It's getting close to crunch time one way or another," he said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended at 2,352.13, barely changed from last Friday's close of 2,351.94.
